01. A COMPLETE APPLICATION PACKET IS REQUIRED FOR EMPLOYMENT CONSIDERATION. A complete application packet includes the following: 1. A complete and detailed Long Beach Community College District Online Employment Application, 2. A current resume or curriculum vitae, 3. A cover letter (if posting requires it), 4. Complete transcripts of ALL lower and upper division and graduate level college/university course work (need not be official). Transcripts from countries other than the United States must be evaluated by an agency that is a member of the National Association of Credentials Evaluation Service (NACES) or Association of International Credential Evaluators, Inc (AICE). if applicable, 5. A list of three references (included on application or uploaded as an attachment) My application packet is complete. I understand that failure to submit a detailed and complete application packet will disqualify me from being considered for this position and once application is submitted no documents can be added afterwards by LBCC staff on your behalf. Options: Yes | No

02. This position requires you to live and be a California resident. If you currently live outside of California, if offered the position, are you willing to relocate? Options: Yes | No | I am a California resident

03. PLEASE NOTE*** Email notices will be sent to the email address on this application. Applicants should check both their email inbox and spam/junk folder for notices. It is your responsibility, as the applicant to provide the correct contact information by which to be notified. Failure to provide the correct contact information on your application, including not properly filling out any portion of the application correctly or failure to participate in any portion of the examination process will result in termination from the recruitment process. Options: I have read, understand and agree with this passage
Possession of a master's degree, and

Student services procedures, including orientation procedures, placement services, counseling and educational planning, enrollment services and procedures, referrals to specialized support services, CCAP partnership agreements, high school articulation processes, and LBCC instructional programs.
One year of formal training, internship, or leadership experience reasonably related to the administrative assignment.
Three or more years of experience focused on matriculation and dual enrollment programs.
Evidence of experience in the areas of organization, planning, development, staffing, budget management, evaluation, and supervision reasonably related to the administrative assignment

Plan and direct day-to-day operations and activities for Matriculation and Early College Initiatives, ensuring full compliance with state regulations and district policies. Hire, train, supervise, and evaluate program personnel.
Lead annual program planning for Matriculation and Early College Initiatives.
Cultivate and sustain relationships with local K-12 partners that advance matriculation and dual enrollment, and support the expansion of Viking Advantage and the Long Beach College Promise.

Develop and update CCAPs, MOUs, and articulation agreements in coordination with K-12 administrators and key stakeholders; prepare and submit annual CCAP reporting to the California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office.
Partner with internal and external stakeholders to grow dual enrollment, build CCAP pathways, maintain strong course success rates, and increase completion of 12+ units before high school graduation.

Collaborate with deans and department chairs to establish program timelines, coordinate course offerings, and secure faculty assignments; develop and maintain the faculty handbook and related onboarding materials; provide ongoing communication and support to participating instructors; and address issues affecting faculty and students.
Regularly convene the Dual Enrollment Workgroup.

Work closely with the Matriculation Coordinator, Dual Enrollment Counselor, and Counseling department heads to provide educational plans and counseling support for matriculation and dual enrollment students both on campus and at high school sites.
Update new student orientation, website content, and related program resources to maintain compliance with Title 5 and other legislative requirements by established deadlines.

Coordinate year-round program services and events, including but not limited to the High School Educator Conference, Express Days, Viking Preview Day, Viking Summer Voyage, Viking Scholars Award Ceremony, Welcome Day, Family Nights, live orientation, and group counseling.
Analyze disaggregated student data on an ongoing basis to identify equity gaps, and implement case management and targeted interventions that improve matriculation conversion and course success.

Foster strong communication and collaboration with Enrollment Services, Counseling, First-Year Experience, Disabled Student Programs and Services, learning communities, and other student services to remove barriers and promote student success.
Develop, monitor, and administer program budgets; coordinate expenditures and maximize financial resources across multiple funding sources
Administer grants, including contract execution, budget development and monitoring, grant activity management, reporting, and invoicing for program expenditures.

Monitor state and federal regulations and trends affecting dual enrollment and matriculation; interpret requirements for staff, faculty, administrators, and K-12 partners and provide guidance through professional development and ongoing communication.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing using interpersonal skills with tact, patience, and diplomacy.

Work with Information Technology (IITS), Institutional Effectiveness and other District personnel on a continual basis to assist in improving processes; measure effectiveness, and provide the most accurate data to reporting agencies (e.g. California Community College Chancellor's Office).
Participate in evening or weekend activities as required to support program and institutional needs.
Performs other related duties as assigned that support the objective of the position.
Practical and operational understanding of dual enrollment, outreach, and matriculation services

Federal and state laws and regulations, and district policies related to student services and programs, including but not limited to State Education Code sections, Student Equity and Achievement (SEA) Program, AB 19, AB 705, AB 1705, AB 1805, AB 132, AB 288, SB 1244, SB 554, Americans with Disabilities Act, Dream Act, FERPA, Title IV, Title IX, the and other legislative bills, regulations, policies, and procedures.

Work effectively with faculty, management, staff, and students to promote access and equity; work cooperatively and coordinate projects with other institutional stakeholders to offer effective services to students.
Demonstrated advocacy for students and student needs.
Budget preparation, reporting, and administration for programs, including grant-funded programs, and audit response procedures for district, state, and federal requirements.
Interpret, apply, and effectively explain rules, regulations, policies, and procedures.
Staff and faculty collaboration with full consideration for bargaining units, agreements, and employment laws.
Manage multiple projects while meeting schedules and timelines.
Supervision and leadership that models collaboration, inclusivity, and a culture of care.
Analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action.
Digital tools that are essential for project management, outreach, and academic case management
Create goals, outcomes, and measurable metrics to assess outcomes as part of the planning process.
Apply current and emerging information, networking, and instructional technologies
Supervise and evaluate staff directing them appropriately in developing best practices in a teamwork environment.
Actively promote, encourage, and support faculty development, and encourage and promote innovation and success.
Work a flexible schedule that includes travel and working evenings and weekends.
Effective oral and written communication and organizational skills

Exhibit and promote a commitment and sensitivity to, and respect for, the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, gender, cultural, disability, and religious backgrounds and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty, and staff, as well as a commitment to integrating diversity into the College's instructional program.
Demonstrated knowledge of Federal, State and institutional programs
Represent the College in a highly professional manner, including clear communication through writing and speaking, with the ability to develop and deliver professional presentations.
Demonstrated ability to manage financial resources with a record of fiscal responsibility and accountability
Apply and use effective interpersonal skills
Demonstrated ability to problem solve and make timely, fair, and equitable decisions
